body:
Examples of frequently asked questions for a service website: 25 templates. GOAI's 2026 editorial selection helps you prepare answers about your offering and working together, using your business's real information.

These frequently asked questions for a service website are templates to adapt. Check the answers against your commercial proposal and business procedures before publishing.

Examples of frequently asked questions for a service website: 25 templates

An FAQ section can explain what customers receive, how to request a quote and where to report a problem. In the CMS, link answers to the service pages and current contact information.

The templates below are GOAI editorial suggestions, with no claim that they come from real customer conversations. The information about Google was checked on 14 September 2026.

What has changed in Google's FAQ displays

According to the official Google Search Central changelog, FAQ rich results have no longer appeared in Google Search since 7 May 2026. Google recorded the removal of the feature's documentation on 15 June 2026.

The old rule, which limited these displays to certain government and health websites, no longer describes the current situation. Keep useful questions on your website without promising that they will appear below the Google result.

The FAQPage type exists in the Schema.org vocabulary and describes a page with frequently asked questions. The existence of this type in the vocabulary is separate from the availability of a feature in Google Search.

How to choose questions for your own business

GOAI's editorial recommendation is to start with messages received through the contact form and questions recorded in discussions about quotes. Remove personal data from the file used for drafting and keep only the issue you need to explain.

  • Group questions about the same service and merge wording that calls for the same answer.
  • Check the answer with the person who sets the quote or carries out the service.
  • Record the internal document supporting the published deadline, price or condition.
  • Decide who updates the answer when the procedure changes.

You can also use the queries available in Search Console to identify topics to check with the team. Consult the Google Search Console guide, then compare the selected wording against the services you actually offer.

Question and answer templates by topic

In this GOAI selection, written in 2026, text in square brackets must be replaced with the business's verified information. Publish a template only if it describes your procedure, and remove questions that do not apply.

Services and working process

For this section, use the list of activities in the commercial proposal and the stages confirmed by the person responsible. The answer template should show what working together involves for the customer.

  • What does the service include? Template: "The service includes [confirmed activities], and at the end you receive [documents or materials delivered]. The proposal describes optional activities separately, along with the conditions under which they can be requested."
  • How long does the work take? Template: "The estimated deadline is [verified deadline], calculated from [starting condition]. The schedule may be revised if [situation covered by the procedure], and the change is communicated to you through [channel used]."
  • What should I prepare before work begins? Template: "We need [required materials] and confirmation of [relevant decision]. The contact person checks the documents received and tells you what is missing before scheduling the work."
  • Can I request changes along the way? Template: "Send the request through [agreed channel], with a description of the change. We assess its effect on the activities and explain [actual procedure for approving the cost and deadline]."
  • Is the service suitable for a small business? Template: "We can take on projects that meet [actual acceptance conditions]. To check suitability, we ask you for [required information] before preparing the proposal."

Price and documents for working together

Check these answers against the current proposal and approved commercial documents. Avoid turning a template into a contractual condition that the business does not apply.

  • How is the price determined? Template: "We calculate the quote based on [criteria used], after checking [required information]. You will receive a description of the included activities and how additional requests are handled."
  • Which costs are not included? Template: "The quote does not include [costs actually excluded]. For [optional services], we communicate the price separately and request approval according to the procedure for working together."
  • How is payment made? Template: "Payment is made through [accepted methods], according to [stages specified in the proposal]. The documents sent specify the amount and deadline applicable to each stage."
  • Which documents do I receive? Template: "For our work together, we send you [documents actually issued]. If you have additional administrative requirements, communicate them through [contact channel] before accepting the proposal."
  • What happens if I want to end our work together? Template: "Communicate your request through [specified channel], according to the accepted conditions. We explain the status of the work completed and the closing steps applicable to your agreement."

Delivery and checking the result

Use the acceptance procedure and list of delivered materials for this group of questions. For SEO services, describe the activities and checks without promising guaranteed Google rankings.

  • How do I check the delivered work? Template: "At handover, you receive [actual materials] and the explanations needed to check them. We use [agreed criteria] to identify any differences from the approved requirements."
  • When can I assess the effects of the service? Template: "For [the service concerned], we track [relevant indicators] according to [agreed schedule]. The report explains the observations and limitations of the available data without turning estimates into guaranteed results."
  • How do I request a fix? Template: "Describe the problem through [agreed channel] and include [information needed for checking]. We assess the request against the agreed work and explain the applicable steps."
  • Do I receive progress updates? Template: "We communicate the status through [channel used], at [confirmed times]. The update includes completed activities and decisions for which we need your response."
  • Where can I see similar work? Template: "The examples we can publish are available on [actual portfolio page]. For each project, we specify the service provided and the information we are entitled to present."

Platforms and access

For these templates, check the technical procedure and the record of accounts used in the project. For a WordPress project, describe the permissions needed according to the work involved.

  • What access do I need to provide? Template: "For [specific activity], we request access to [required system], with [justified permissions]. We explain how to grant access before the work begins."
  • Do you work with my platform? Template: "We can work on [platforms confirmed by the team]. For other systems, we check the requirements and tell you whether we can take on the work before accepting the order."
  • How are accounts managed? Template: "The accounts used for the project are managed according to [actual procedure]. At the end, we provide the list of access permissions to check and explain responsibility for keeping or revoking them."
  • How do you send project documents? Template: "We use [approved channel] for the documents needed for our work together. The team specifies which information is needed and how materials requiring restricted access should be sent."
  • What do I receive at the end of our work together? Template: "Handover includes [files and documents specified in the agreement]. For components used under a licence, we explain the applicable conditions and management responsibilities."

Communication and support

Compare the answers against the hours published on the contact page and the support procedure. Fill each template with a real channel, verified before publication.

  • Who is responsible for the project? Template: "The contact person for our work together is [confirmed name or role]. They receive requests and communicate information that needs to be checked by the delivery team."
  • Which channel do we use to talk? Template: "For routine requests, we use [agreed channel]. Documents and approvals are retained through [method used], so that the decision history can be consulted."
  • When will I receive a reply to my message? Template: "Messages are handled during [actual hours], according to [committed response time, if any]. Requests requiring technical checks receive information about the next step through [channel used]."
  • Is support available outside working hours? Template: "Outside working hours, [business's actual policy] applies. For situations covered by this procedure, use [dedicated channel] and provide the requested information."
  • How do I report a problem after handover? Template: "Send the request through [actual form or address], with a description of the problem and when it appeared. We tell you whether the check falls within the agreed service or requires a separate quote."

How to turn templates into publishable answers

Before entering the text into the CMS, replace all fields in brackets and check each condition with the service manager. For deadlines or prices, keep the internal source and confirmation date in the editorial record.

The delivery template should not be filled with a time frame chosen because it sounds convenient. Use the schedule applicable to the service and explain when the deadline calculation begins.

To organise the review, use the SEO brief for writers. If the answer introduces the team or its responsibilities, keep it consistent with the business's About page.

What to check in markup and AI visibility

Google's rules for structured data require markup to describe the page content and not mislead. An error in the markup does not automatically mean the entire page is removed from search.

A structured data validator can help check the markup, but validation does not reactivate the retired FAQ feature. If a WordPress module generates FAQPage, check its role separately before changing the configuration.

Do not replace FAQPage with QAPage in an attempt to recover those displays: Google's QAPage documentation excludes FAQ pages written by the business without the ability for users to add alternative answers. The type must be chosen according to the actual content and the feature's rules.

For AI Overviews and AI Mode, Google states that no special markup is needed. A question-and-answer format does not guarantee that the page will be cited in AI answers.

Publishing and maintaining the FAQ section

In the CMS, place specific questions beside the description of the service they concern. For shared procedures, you can use a central page with links from relevant pages, avoiding contradictory answers.

  1. Check that answers are readable on a phone and questions are grouped by topic.
  2. Test links to services and the contact form.
  3. Remove unfilled fields and unconfirmed conditions.
  4. Review the answers when you change the offering or support procedure.

Readers should be able to submit a request even when their answer is not in the list. Include a visible link to the contact page, with the information needed to continue the discussion.

To check page structure and access to content, consult GOAI's technical SEOservice. To review content and links between pages, check the activities included in the SEO optimisation services.
